title: Mía and the Travelling Cloud
summary: Mía misses her grandma terribly. She lives far away, by the sea. One afternoon, a cloud stops at Mía’s balcony and invites her to climb on.

scenes.text:
Mía was six years old, with two brown plaits and a balcony on the seventh floor.

From her balcony you could see a huge piece of sky. And what Mía liked best in the whole world was watching the clouds. That one looked like a rabbit. That one, a boat. That one over there, her grandma's face.

Her grandma, Nena, lived very far away, by the sea, in a house with a red roof. Mía hadn't seen her since the summer. And she missed her so much that sometimes it made her tummy ache.

One afternoon, while she was having her snack, she saw something that made her put down her biscuit half-eaten.

A round cloud, white and soft, was floating slowly down towards her balcony. And it stopped there, hovering just in front of the railing.

And it smiled at her.

Mía went out onto the balcony with her eyes wide open.

"You can smile?" she asked.

The cloud wobbled its whole round body, as if to say yes. Then it came down a little, until it was resting on the balcony floor, as soft as a cushion.

"Do you want me to climb on?"

Mía hesitated for a second. Then two. And then she remembered all the times she had dreamed of touching a cloud.

She climbed on very carefully. The cloud was warm and it tickled her legs, and out came a giggle.

"Hello, Mía," said the cloud, in a voice like a pillow. "Where would you like to go?"

Mía didn't have to think about it.

"To my grandma's house."

And up went the cloud.

Slowly at first, then faster, until Mía's building was tiny, like a matchbox.

They flew over the city. From up there, the cars looked like ants with lights, and the streets looked like lines in a drawing.

They flew over a river that shone like a silver ribbon. Over green and yellow fields, stitched together like a patchwork quilt. Over mountains with snow on their tips.

And then they passed right under a rainbow. So close that Mía reached out her hand, and her fingers came back coloured.

Mía laughed. The breeze was tickling her cheeks.

On the other side of the mountains, the sea appeared. Blue, enormous, shining.

And on the shore, very small, a house with a red roof.

"That's it!" shouted Mía.

The cloud floated a little lower. In the garden was Grandma Nena, hanging white sheets on the line. Above the roof flew the seagulls.

And then Grandma looked up, saw the cloud… and waved.

The way she always did with every cloud. Just in case.

"Grandma!" shouted Mía, waving both arms. "Grandma, it's me!"

The wind carried her voice away. But Grandma stood looking up for a long while, with her hand on her heart, smiling.

When the sun began to go down, the cloud said:

"It's time to go back."

They flew home over the sea, over the mountains, over the river, while the sky turned orange and pink. The city appeared below, with its windows lighting up one by one.

The cloud set Mía down on her balcony, very carefully, and floated slowly away, until it was lost among all the others.

That night, when Mía was already in bed, the phone rang.

It was Grandma Nena.

"Do you know something?" she said. "Today a cloud went past here shaped like a little girl. With two plaits. And I could have sworn it waved at me."

Mía smiled in the dark.

And she fell asleep hugging her pillow, which was almost, almost as soft as a cloud.
